quotes.text: If a measure changes visibility, rows, columns, or classification, it is acting as an access control that belongs to identity, not DAX. If you remember nothing else, remember this. DAX must never decide who can see data identity must.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core rule that authorization belongs to identity, not to DAX measures.

quotes.text: Lineage is evidence, not assurance. It's post facto storytelling. It can tell you where data moved. It cannot tell you whether your policies were enforced when it moved
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates lineage as documentation from enforcement as a control.

quotes.text: Cross workspace reuse is not a convenience feature. It's an access plane. When you point a report in workspace B at a model in workspace A, you didn't just reuse metrics.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes shared datasets as an authorization surface rather than a productivity feature.

quotes.text: Capacity isolation is cheaper than incident response. You trade a modest baseline cost for predictable containment, faster investigations and fewer late night bridge calls.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete cost argument for separating capacities by risk domain.

quotes.text: Training does not intercept that moment. Controls do. The system either evaluates identity and labels before the measure exists or it accepts whatever the author can imagine.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why enforced controls beat training for keeping models from drifting.

Entra, Purview, DLP and capacity as controls

takeaways: DAX should only express analytics; any logic that changes who can see or infer data belongs to identity in Microsoft Entra, not to measures.
Business definitions, keys and cross-boundary benchmarks must live upstream with Purview labels and DLP that can actually block exports, blends and notebook writes.
Lineage and training are evidence and explanation, while enforced vetoes, enumerated Entra groups and capacity isolation are what keep Fabric models from drifting.
hook: Row-level security works in the demo, yet your Fabric model can still leak through measures, calculated tables and shared datasets. This episode is for Power BI and Fabric architects who need governance that holds under deadline pressure. You get five failure modes and a deterministic playbook built on Entra, Purview, DLP and capacity isolation.
